script: Why did the movers find a locked door inside my new house that wasn't on any blueprint? But the realtor swore she didn't know it existed. Because the seller had blacked it out of every disclosure. It was behind a false wall in the basement, sealed with six deadbolts from the inside. A locksmith needed four hours to get through all of them. Inside was a single room with a cot, a chair, and a wall covered floor to ceiling in photographs. Every photograph was of the house itself, taken from across the street, dated over eleven years. The most recent one was taken two days before I moved in. I called the police, and they told me the seller had a restraining order filed against him in another state. Filed by the woman who owned this house before her. Nobody had ever told the buyers before us, because nobody was required to. And the question the whole street still won't answer out loud is the one I keep coming back to.
